policy.purpose: Permanent replayable R5 regression ownership without patient dialogue or runtime secrets.
policy.fixedRule: Fixed requires a confirmed root cause, full fix SHA, and an existing permanent regression.
policy.humanBugRule: A human bug remains open until symptom, exact root cause, replay, fix SHA, evidence, and permanent gate are recorded.
policy.privacyRule: Never store patient dialogue, prompts, reasoning, bearer values, state-token values, usernames, or complete user paths.
policy.frozenBoundary: Never change data/**, medical facts, review states, scoring contracts, or frozen R4.1/R5 artifacts for test convenience.

entries.title: Stage 3 sparse-evidence dead end
entries.userVisibleSymptom: Stage 2 can be submitted with too little usable evidence, after which stage 3 cannot be completed and the learner cannot return to collect evidence.

rootCause.detail: Submission locking and stage-3 eligibility were validated independently, allowing a locked state with neither sufficient evidence nor a recovery action.

minimumReproduction.environment: Deterministic seven-stage runner with sparse evidence
steps: Initialize P001 in free mode.
Submit stages 1 and 2 below the stage-3 evidence requirement.
Verify a legal recovery action remains available.

entries.legacyGap: The 42-case flow used empty fixed submissions and proved endpoint order, not evidence sufficiency or recoverability.

entries.title: Random mode was sent to the durable-attempt API
entries.userVisibleSymptom: Random training opened, but durable initialization returned HTTP 400 and later saves were not durable.

rootCause.detail: The renderer sent UI mode random to an endpoint accepting only free, osce, or rct, and initialization recovered from 404 but not that 400.

minimumReproduction.environment: Mode-contract test
steps: Create random attempt identity.
Resolve its durable mode.
Assert the request uses free while UI identity remains random.

entries.legacyGap: Renderer E2E used an in-memory bridge while sidecar acceptance bypassed the renderer, so incompatible mode vocabularies both passed.

entries.title: Renderer autosave did not reach durable state
entries.userVisibleSymptom: The window appeared usable, but closing and reopening lost recent questions and stage progress.

rootCause.detail: Durable initialization failed before a server row existed while the renderer continued with volatile state and tests observed only mocked save calls.

minimumReproduction.environment: Real renderer, sidecar, and temporary SQLite
steps: Initialize a fresh attempt.
Change state and wait for save acknowledgement.
Recreate the renderer and load from SQLite.

entries.legacyGap: The browser bridge persisted to a Map and desktop acceptance used direct HTTP without the real client save lifecycle.

entries.title: Packaged backend passed while the Tauri window failed
entries.userVisibleSymptom: Direct backend diagnostics passed, but the real window could not initialize or persist an attempt.

rootCause.detail: Automation launched the sidecar directly and never exercised Tauri resources, runtime injection, WebView2, renderer, SQLite, and normal close as one chain.

minimumReproduction.environment: Tauri no-bundle executable with test-only WebView2 CDP
steps: Launch real Tauri with an isolated profile.
Save through the visible renderer.
Close normally, restart, restore, and verify cleanup.

entries.legacyGap: Source renderer and packaged-sidecar tests covered disjoint halves of the product.

entries.title: New stage inherited the previous scroll position
entries.userVisibleSymptom: After advancing, the learner landed partway down the new stage and could miss its title and instructions.

rootCause.detail: The persistent scroll container was reused without resetting its position when active stage changed.

minimumReproduction.environment: 390 by 844 and 1093 by 614 viewports
steps: Scroll to the bottom of a long stage.
Advance.
Assert the responsible container starts at the top.

entries.legacyGap: Screenshots inspected settled layouts but did not execute scroll-then-transition.

entries.title: Fixed action area obscured content
entries.userVisibleSymptom: At short desktop or mobile heights, the action area covered inputs or the last content row.

rootCause.detail: Sticky positioning and bottom spacing were checked separately, allowing action and content regions to overlap.

minimumReproduction.environment: Short desktop and mobile viewports with long bilingual text
steps: Open a long form.
Scroll every focusable control into view.
Assert no rectangle intersects the sticky action region.

entries.legacyGap: Static geometry checks did not compare every focusable control after scrolling.

entries.title: Language switching lost keyboard focus
entries.userVisibleSymptom: Switching Chinese and English moved focus, forcing keyboard users to restart navigation or type into the wrong control.

rootCause.detail: Language rerender replaced or reordered the focused subtree without a focus-restoration contract.

minimumReproduction.environment: Desktop and mobile renderer with keyboard input
steps: Focus the primary input.
Switch language by keyboard.
Assert focus remains on the equivalent control and accepts one input.

entries.legacyGap: Language tests asserted text, not activeElement and post-switch typing.

entries.title: R4 and R5 installation or data identity can collide
entries.userVisibleSymptom: Installing, running, or uninstalling R5 can overwrite or remove R4 state or installation metadata.

rootCause.detail: The Phase 3 start configuration shared R4 product name, version, identifier, and install mode; R5 now has a distinct static identity while real coexistence remains externally blocked.

minimumReproduction.environment: Disposable Windows VM with frozen R4 installed
steps: Create R4 durable state.
Install and run R5.
Uninstall each product independently and verify the other state remains.

entries.legacyGap: Data-directory names were validated without side-by-side Windows installation identity.

entries.title: Unicode, spaces, and long paths were not portable
entries.userVisibleSymptom: Preparation or startup succeeds on the developer computer but fails under a Chinese, spaced, or deeply nested path.

rootCause.detail: Earlier readiness relied on an ASCII repository path and host tooling, leaving path-safe argument passing and bundled-resource discovery unexercised.

minimumReproduction.environment: Scratch package copy under a Chinese spaced near-long path
steps: Copy without renaming frozen artifacts.
Launch as a standard user without host Node.
Save, close, reopen, and export diagnostics.

entries.legacyGap: Local tests reused the repository path and installed development runtime.

entries.title: Required packaged runtime resource is missing
entries.userVisibleSymptom: The backend cannot start and the app must show an actionable safe diagnostic instead of a blank or hanging window.

rootCause.detail: The injected cause is removal of one required resource from a scratch package copy.

minimumReproduction.environment: Scratch staged-resource copy
steps: Remove one required resource.
Launch.
Assert fail-closed classification, no secret leakage, and no process residue.

entries.legacyGap: Bundle scans prove presence in one artifact but not visible recovery after loss or quarantine.

entries.title: Local model is missing or fails its hash contract
entries.userVisibleSymptom: Preparation fails or silently runs a different model when the expected model is absent, partial, or corrupt.

rootCause.detail: The scenarios inject an absent model and a mismatched digest in an isolated R5 data directory.

minimumReproduction.environment: Isolated R5 model directory
steps: Run without a model.
Run with a wrong-digest same-name file.
Assert safe fallback or actionable failure, correct label, and zero cloud requests.

entries.legacyGap: Optional real-model tests did not exercise corrupt or absent model recovery through the visible app.

entries.title: SQLite is locked or corrupt
entries.userVisibleSymptom: Preparation or save fails; the app must not delete the database, report success, or strand processes.

rootCause.detail: Tests use a real exclusive SQLite lock and a corrupt scratch database rather than fabricated error text.

minimumReproduction.environment: Temporary R5 SQLite database
steps: Hold an exclusive lock and attempt save.
Repeat with a corrupt copy.
Verify classification, no deletion, and recovery after lock release.

entries.legacyGap: Compatibility tests supplied synthetic labels instead of provoking real SQLite errors.

entries.title: Repeated preparation can race or duplicate runtime work
entries.userVisibleSymptom: Rapid repeated prepare actions can leave duplicate progress, an unresponsive action, or orphaned processes.

rootCause.detail: No production trace identifies whether renderer, Tauri command, sidecar startup, or model installer owns the suspected race.

minimumReproduction.environment: Real Tauri with deterministic delayed preparation
steps: Trigger prepare ten times rapidly.
Wait for one terminal result.
Assert one runtime, one state transition, and no residue.

entries.legacyGap: Lifecycle tests invoke prepare once and wait before another action.

entries.title: A second case can inherit first-case state
entries.userVisibleSymptom: Another case can show the previous case language, answers, stage, evidence, or report.

rootCause.detail: Attempt identity includes case, language, and mode, but browser state and SQLite isolation were never asserted together across a case switch.

minimumReproduction.environment: Real renderer, sidecar, and SQLite
steps: Save P001 Chinese free progress.
Save P003 English random progress.
Return to P001 and assert each attempt has only its own state.

entries.legacyGap: Pure identity and direct-sidecar tests omitted renderer caches and SQLite authority together.

entries.title: Normal close and reopen does not restore authority
entries.userVisibleSymptom: Progress appears saved until the desktop process closes, then disappears or duplicates after reopening.

rootCause.detail: Browser reload and direct sidecar restart substituted for the real Tauri close handler, process cleanup, WebView profile, and SQLite reopen.

minimumReproduction.environment: Tauri no-bundle with persistent isolated R5 directories
steps: Save visible state.
Close normally and wait for the process tree.
Restart and verify one restored attempt and revision.

entries.legacyGap: No permanent test sends normal close to a real Tauri window and reconnects after full exit.

entries.title: Student output exposes internal fields
entries.userVisibleSymptom: A learner can see teacher-only diagnosis, scoring, provenance, intent, agent, review, or workflow fields in API, DOM, clipboard, or export.

rootCause.detail: This permanent privacy invariant applies explicit allowlists at server projection and every student output channel.

minimumReproduction.environment: Student session across all output channels
steps: Complete representative stages.
Capture student-authorized output.
Assert the allowlist and absence of internal field families.

entries.legacyGap: Existing checks cover selected responses or static output, not every channel after a full desktop journey.

entries.title: Stage 7 exposes internal 360-point score
entries.userVisibleSymptom: The learner can see the internal raw score or its private component breakdown.

rootCause.detail: The server-authoritative score must be projected to the approved student scale before every student-facing output.

minimumReproduction.environment: Completed stage-7 student attempt
steps: Complete seven stages.
Inspect API, DOM, clipboard, and export.
Assert approved projection and absence of internal raw fields.

entries.legacyGap: Projection tests did not prove every stage-7 desktop channel uses the projection.

entries.title: Desktop training sends a cloud request
entries.userVisibleSymptom: A desktop action contacts a non-loopback service, violating the offline and privacy promise.

rootCause.detail: Zero cloud requests is a permanent runtime invariant at sidecar authority and test-process network boundaries.

minimumReproduction.environment: Canonical Tauri journey with loopback instrumentation
steps: Perform representative actions.
Exercise safe fallback.
Assert cloud count is zero and no non-loopback connection occurred.

entries.legacyGap: Direct backend counters omitted requests initiated by the packaged WebView.

entries.title: Rule fallback is labeled local AI
entries.userVisibleSymptom: When the model is unavailable, the UI claims local AI produced a rule-fallback response.

rootCause.detail: Serving-mode labels must derive from runtime evidence, not requested mode or HTTP success.

minimumReproduction.environment: Real renderer with deterministic model-start failure
steps: Force safe model failure.
Perform a supported action.
Assert fact-bound output and safe-fallback label, never local AI.

entries.legacyGap: Backend fallback and visible labels were tested separately.

entries.title: Child processes or ports remain after close
entries.userVisibleSymptom: After closing, sidecar or model processes retain memory or ports and can break the next launch.

rootCause.detail: Zero residual process and port state is checked after normal close and repeated cycles.

minimumReproduction.environment: Real Tauri with sidecar and deterministic model
steps: Launch and close normally ten times.
Inspect child PIDs and ports after each exit.
Assert all are gone before next launch.

entries.legacyGap: Direct lifecycle tests do not prove real window close releases the Job Object and CDP port.

entries.title: Old WebView cache conflicts with fresh SQLite
entries.userVisibleSymptom: A fresh data store opens with old stage state or initialization fails because cached identity disagrees with SQLite.

rootCause.detail: WebView storage and SQLite were tested independently; no test retained the old profile while replacing the authoritative database.

minimumReproduction.environment: Persistent WebView profile with replaceable temporary SQLite
steps: Cache a durable attempt.
Replace only SQLite with a fresh store.
Restart and assert bootstrap clears incompatible cache and creates coherent authority.

entries.legacyGap: State-authority tests used MemoryStorage instead of real WebView profile plus replaced database.

entries.title: Product HEAD authority degrades to desktop-local
entries.userVisibleSymptom: Diagnostics, sidecar, SQLite, and artifact evidence claim different builds, making saved state and evidence untrustworthy.

rootCause.detail: Tauri passes HEMATURIA_PRODUCT_HEAD while SQLite reads NEXT_PUBLIC_GIT_SHA and the sidecar previously defaulted missing values to desktop-local.

minimumReproduction.environment: Staged sidecar and Tauri diagnostic built from a full SHA
steps: Launch with Tauri product-head authority.
Read safe diagnostic and SQLite authority.
Assert both equal artifact HEAD and never desktop-local.

entries.legacyGap: Tests supplied NEXT_PUBLIC_GIT_SHA directly and accepted desktop-local.

entries.title: Installer and runtime use different model directories
entries.userVisibleSymptom: The installer reports success, but the app still reports the model missing.

rootCause.detail: R5 runtime resolves MentorLocalAI-R5 while installer, acceptance, benchmark, or docs retained an older identifier rather than one resolver.

minimumReproduction.environment: Path contract test without model download
steps: Resolve install, runtime, acceptance, and benchmark targets.
Normalize paths.
Assert one R5 models directory.

entries.legacyGap: Each script built its own default path and no shared test compared them.

entries.title: R5 NSIS identity is not isolated from R4
entries.userVisibleSymptom: Windows can treat R5 as an R4 update or let one uninstaller remove the other product.

rootCause.detail: Frozen R4 and the Phase 3 start configuration shared product name, version, identifier, and current-user install mode; static R5 identity is now distinct.

minimumReproduction.environment: Candidate preflight plus disposable Windows VM
steps: Compare frozen R4 and candidate identity fields before build.
Stop if all are equal.
After isolation, install and uninstall both independently in a VM.

entries.legacyGap: Data-directory isolation was used as a proxy for Windows installer identity.

entries.title: Original mentor computer could not prepare and save reliably
entries.userVisibleSymptom: On the original mentor computer, preparation or state saving failed although the developer computer passed.

rootCause.detail: The original trace and equivalent replay are unavailable; mode normalization, security policy, permissions, resources, and SQLite remain distinct hypotheses.

minimumReproduction.environment: Original mentor machine or evidence-equivalent clean Windows with default security
steps: Run diagnostics without developer tools.
Prepare, save, close, and reopen once.
Export only sanitized diagnostics and cleanup facts.

entries.legacyGap: Local success and a different extraction path cannot establish the original-machine root cause.

entries.title: Saved AI mode is overwritten during renderer hydration
entries.userVisibleSymptom: A saved rule-mode preference can silently return to local AI after opening another renderer surface.

rootCause.detail: The persistence effect wrote the default deepseek mode before the mount effect finished reading the saved preference.

minimumReproduction.environment: Real renderer with isolated browser storage
steps: Save rule mode before navigation.
Open a case with a fresh SQLite authority.
Assert the preference remains rule before and after reload.

entries.legacyGap: The preference test was timing-sensitive and prior isolated runs did not trigger the default-state write before hydration.

entries.title: Mentor Full human entrypoint did not load bundled local AI
entries.userVisibleSymptom: After fully extracting the mentor Full package and opening the visible application executable, the window started but the local Qwen service never became ready and the UI reported the model missing.

rootCause.detail: The human report bypassed the package root launcher and opened App/HematuriaTraining-R5.exe directly, so the executable had no bundled-model context and correctly fell back to the R5 data-directory model path. Prior real-model automation injected HEMATURIA_DESKTOP_MODEL_PATH and therefore never tested the human entrypoint. The launcher also depended on CIM/Get-NetTCPConnection, which is not reliable for a standard Windows user; its native replacement initially retained incompatible ProcessId and LocalPort field assumptions until the real long-path replay exposed them.

minimumReproduction.environment: Fresh extraction with scratch R5 data and no desktop model environment variables
steps: Extract the exact Full ZIP once.
Clear desktop model-path, model-mode, and test-mode variables.
Run only the package root launcher and verify the bundled Qwen model becomes ready.

entries.legacyGap: Phase 4 real-model automation supplied HEMATURIA_DESKTOP_MODEL_PATH and launched the application executable directly, so it could pass without proving the package's human entrypoint or bundled model context.

entries.title: Stage 2 selected orders did not return results
entries.userVisibleSymptom: The learner selected investigations and used the main order action, but no result appeared and the training flow could not reliably proceed to diagnostic evidence.

rootCause.detail: Stage 2 checkboxes updated answers.selectedOrders, but the learner-visible primary action called submitOrder(), which read only the separate free-text orderInput and returned before the API call when that field was empty. Existing tests typed free text, clicked a secondary selected-results action, or called the handler directly, so none exercised the real checkbox-to-primary-action path.

minimumReproduction.environment: Real renderer contract with the real training handler
steps: Enter Stage 2 for P001.
Select a reportable order using the catalog checkbox.
Use the primary order action and require exactly one report, evidence item, timeline entry, reload, and restart persistence.

entries.legacyGap: Existing renderer tests either typed free-text orders or used the separate selected-results button, while API tests constructed order actions directly and therefore never exercised the learner's primary click path.

entries.title: Sidecar loopback self-health startup can intermittently prevent desktop runtime injection
entries.userVisibleSymptom: The installed window opens at tauri.localhost but the desktop runtime never becomes available, so training cannot start.

rootCause.detail: Desktop sidecar startup used a single-shot self-loopback health probe as a fatal readiness gate. A transient localhost transport failure therefore terminated an otherwise correctly spawned sidecar before it could publish the ready handshake; diagnostic normalization also collapsed the health-probe failure into unknown_runtime_failure.

minimumReproduction.environment: TEST_MODE health-probe injection plus real-model no-bundle soak
steps: Inject one ECONNREFUSED result into the first sidecar self-health probe.
Observe the historical single-shot gate terminate before publishing the ready handshake.
Run the same injection with the bounded transport-only retry and assert readiness on attempt two.
Inject permanent transport and logical health failures and assert stable fail-closed diagnostics.

entries.legacyGap: The original smoke reported only runtime_missing; the sidecar collapsed connect, timeout, HTTP, payload and status failures into one code, while Tauri lost the loopback_health phase.

entries.title: Mentor launcher model override was ignored when SQLite retained standard mode
entries.userVisibleSymptom: The mentor Full package contains Qwen3-1.7B and launches lightweight mode, but local assistance remains unavailable and diagnostics report the standard Qwen3-4B profile.

rootCause.detail: The sidecar selected the model descriptor only from localAi.modelMode in SQLite and ignored the trusted HEMATURIA_DESKTOP_MODEL_MODE launcher override, so a stale standard preference validated the bundled 1.7B file against the 4B alias, size, and digest.

minimumReproduction.environment: Scratch R5 SQLite plus the mentor launcher model path
steps: Persist localAi.modelMode=standard.
Start the sidecar with HEMATURIA_DESKTOP_MODEL_MODE=lightweight and the bundled 1.7B path.
Assert the effective descriptor remains lightweight and the configured preference remains intact.

entries.legacyGap: The mentor entrypoint test used a fresh scratch SQLite, while real-model acceptance explicitly wrote the requested mode into SQLite; neither replayed an older standard preference with a lightweight package override.

entries.title: Stage 2 exposed governance states and hid existing or shared reports
entries.userVisibleSymptom: After five investigations were ordered, the learner saw awaiting-medical-review text and missing-metadata placeholders, while a repeated or shared result could be summarized as zero returned reports.

rootCause.detail: The training handler returned internal order-outcome objects directly to the learner, report cards converted missing metadata into review placeholders, and duplicate orders were short-circuited before releasedReports could be resurfaced or shared-panel ownership represented.

minimumReproduction.environment: P005 desktop practice attempt
steps: Order urinalysis, urine sediment, urine mycobacteria testing, PSA, and urinary ultrasound.
Inspect the per-order summary and report metadata.
Repeat the same orders and verify the existing report remains visible without a second evidence event.

entries.legacyGap: Prior API tests asserted internal pending states and zero duplicate reports as correct, while renderer tests verified those same governance messages instead of task completion and existing-result visibility.

entries.title: Direct packaged executable did not discover or select the bundled lightweight model
entries.userVisibleSymptom: The extracted Full package opened, but local AI stayed unavailable when the learner launched the App executable directly and SQLite still preferred the absent standard model.

rootCause.detail: Tauri forwarded an explicit model path but not the validated model mode, and the direct executable had no package-root model discovery. The sidecar then honored the stale standard preference even though only the bundled lightweight model was present.

minimumReproduction.environment: Extracted Full package with no model environment variables and scratch SQLite configured for standard
steps: Launch App/HematuriaTraining-R5.exe directly.
Require automatic discovery of Model/Qwen3-1.7B-Q4_K_M.gguf.
Require configured standard but effective lightweight with packaged_model_fallback and local readiness.

entries.legacyGap: The previous package acceptance supplied model environment variables, so it proved the sidecar with a fixture configuration rather than the root launcher and direct executable as humans actually run them.

entries.title: Patient answers exposed chart-like summaries instead of ordinary first-person speech
entries.userVisibleSymptom: A patient answered an open symptom question with a compressed chart phrase such as 'foamy urine, urine-test hematuria with facial rash for two weeks', and known low fever or absent flank pain could become question-shaped uncertainty.

rootCause.detail: The governed answer planner passed legacy source wording directly to the response, while the local model was limited to metadata classification. The deterministic fallback therefore bypassed spoken realization, and narrow fever/flank classifiers failed to recognize existing low-fever and no-flank-pain wording.

minimumReproduction.environment: P035 with local model disabled
steps: Ask the six reported P035 questions.
Observe chart-like chief-complaint wording and question-shaped uncertainty.
Replay twenty fixed natural questions across all 42 cases through the shared spoken realizer.

entries.legacyGap: Existing tests proved intent routing and fact preservation, but accepted chart fragments as valid output and did not assert ordinary first-person speech for a fixed 42-case natural-question corpus.

entries.title: Student catalog offered investigations that were anatomically or physiologically inapplicable
entries.userVisibleSymptom: Learners could order PSA for female cases without prostate anatomy or a pregnancy test for male and explicitly non-pregnancy-potential cases, inviting fabricated negative reports.

rootCause.detail: The catalog applied only partial sex filters and did not share a case-level age, pregnancy-potential, and anatomy applicability predicate across the renderer and training handler.

minimumReproduction.environment: All 42 approved cases and the student order catalog
steps: Enumerate every case and catalog order.
Apply sex, age, pregnancy-potential, anatomy, and declared prerequisite rules.
Assert every inapplicable case-order is absent before ordering and no applicable order is hidden.

entries.legacyGap: The prior 2742-order audit treated selectability as fixed and therefore tried to manufacture terminal outcomes for medically inapplicable combinations instead of auditing the catalog boundary.

entries.title: Medically applicable selectable orders could end without a visible report card
entries.userVisibleSymptom: A learner could select an applicable investigation and receive a blank, unavailable, not-performed, or review-waiting state instead of a hospital-style report card.

rootCause.detail: The result projection covered approved source mappings but left the remaining applicable case-order combinations in governance placeholders; no deterministic case-specific teaching report layer completed the student-visible contract.

minimumReproduction.environment: All 42 approved cases after applicability filtering
steps: Order every selectable investigation for every case.
Require a non-empty visible report card for each case-order.
Replay and restart, then assert deterministic content, no duplicate event, no cross-case leakage, and no diagnostic or scoring eligibility.

entries.legacyGap: Earlier tests validated a small approved mapping set and accepted no-result or review placeholders as terminal, so they did not prove task completion for every selectable case-order combination.

entries.title: Natural prior-care questions fell through to generic patient unknown
entries.userVisibleSymptom: A learner could ask ordinary variants about prior visits or investigations even when the case contained answerable facts, yet the patient repeatedly returned a generic memory failure.

rootCause.detail: The governed Patient Agent ontology covered fixed symptom and history prompts but had no shared semantic domains for prior visits, investigations, prior results, treatment, current-problem medication, or treatment response; unmatched wording therefore reached the generic fallback.

minimumReproduction.environment: Case P031 in a real Patient Session with provider disabled
steps: Ask multiple natural variants about prior investigations.
Observe the generic unknown despite source-backed urine and ultrasound facts.
Replay context and compound follow-ups through the same session entrypoint.

entries.legacyGap: The previous 42-case suite repeated a fixed twenty-question inventory and proved wording realism only after routing, so it never exercised the missing semantic families or context-dependent follow-ups.

entries.title: Patient prior-care answers lacked a source-bounded knowledge layer
entries.userVisibleSymptom: Known prior tests could be omitted while current encounters, absent treatment, or unrelated history risked being projected as answerable patient facts.

rootCause.detail: Patient routing had no dedicated fail-closed projection between repository case facts and answer plans. Broad narrative matching could not distinguish a current visit from a prior visit, a treatment denial from treatment response, or slot-specific output permissions.

minimumReproduction.environment: All 42 cases plus P001, P018, P020, P022, and P031 boundary fixtures
steps: Project seven prior-care domains for every case.
Require source-backed facts or explicit missing states.
Inject teacher-only and Stage 2 sentinel fields and require zero projection.
Generate five hundred replayable non-fixture questions and compare grounded plans.

entries.legacyGap: Existing tests treated non-empty output as success and did not independently assert current-versus-prior visit, negated treatment, teacher-field exclusion, slot-level vocabulary isolation, or answerable generic-unknown counts.

entries.title: Local AI control envelopes were rendered as patient speech
entries.userVisibleSymptom: A learner could see a JSON object and internal field name around an otherwise ordinary patient answer in the conversation UI.

rootCause.detail: Patient naturalization validated governed-answer preservation before proving the provider output was plain patient-visible text. A JSON control envelope containing the governed answer therefore passed substring preservation, was counted as accepted local AI, and reached the public reply and renderer unchanged.

minimumReproduction.environment: Synthetic local loopback provider plus the real Patient Session and renderer
steps: Return JSON, fenced JSON, role envelopes, quoted control keys, and embedded object or array fragments from the provider.
Require at most one plain-text correction.
Reject a second invalid response to the deterministic grounded fallback.
Assert public reply, UI, restored messages, and timeline contain no internal protocol text.

entries.legacyGap: Existing tests checked medical wording and governed fact preservation but did not validate the provider output shape before preservation or replay malformed accepted output through the public API, renderer, and persisted state.

entries.title: The renderer blocked valid grounded compound patient answers
entries.userVisibleSymptom: A learner asked about hypertension, diabetes, and medication together, but the UI replaced the complete grounded patient answer with a generic clarification message.

rootCause.detail: The renderer safety guard inferred a single topic from the question and treated every other protected topic in the reply as contamination. It did not scope the check to all topics explicitly asked or authorized by the public grounded matchedFacts and matchedSlotIds returned for that turn.

minimumReproduction.environment: Real ClinicalTrainingClient with a public Patient reply
steps: Ask one question containing hypertension, diabetes, and medication clauses.
Return the grounded answer with the corresponding public slot and fact identifiers.
Require the complete answer on initial submit and reconnect.
Ask a single-topic control question and require ungrounded extra topics to remain blocked.

entries.legacyGap: Backend compound tests proved every grounded child fact was present, while renderer safety tests covered only single-topic contamination; no test required the real UI to preserve a multi-topic grounded reply through submit, reconnect, and autosave.

entries.title: Student Patient API exposed internal governance and runtime diagnostics
entries.userVisibleSymptom: A learner-facing Patient response could contain teacher-only key names and raw medical-review reason codes even when the spoken answer itself was safe.

rootCause.detail: The Patient endpoint manually serialized a mixed response containing both renderer fields and internal governance, provider, model, classification, source, and reasoning diagnostics. The renderer then depended on a raw internal fallback reason instead of a stable public state, while the existing response allowlist explicitly permitted the diagnostic fields.

minimumReproduction.environment: Real Patient handler with an authorized session and a medically quarantined history clause
steps: Issue a normal student Patient request that contains one medically quarantined clause and other allowed clauses.
Inspect the complete public JSON response.
Observe internal teacher-only and medical-review identifiers in the historical payload.
Replay normal, governed, safety, unavailable, and protocol-correction paths through the strict Student DTO gate.

entries.legacyGap: The old API test treated governance and runtime diagnostics as approved Student fields, and package acceptance audited rendered text without recursively auditing the complete public Patient JSON.
